title: SafetyClaimVerify: An NLP Pipeline for Automatically Fact-Checking AI Safety Claims

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: automated claim verification directly enables accountability infrastructure. A working prototype would demonstrate feasibility and surface unverifiable claims, both valuable for governance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a multi-stage NLP pipeline (extraction, classification, evidence search, verdict) requires advanced software engineering and NLP skills beyond beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four-component pipeline (extraction, classification, evidence search, verification) is too broad for 30 hours. Each component alone could be a project.

novelty.reasoning: The general automated fact-checking pipeline is extensively studied. While applying it specifically to AI safety claims adds a domain twist, the core NLP pipeline architecture (extraction, classification, evidence search, verdict) is well-established with multiple implementations. The AI-safety-specific application is the only novel angle.

evidence: Guo et al. (2022) 'A Survey on Automated Fact-Checking' in TACL provides a comprehensive framework for multi-stage NLP fact-checking pipelines (claim detection, evidence retrieval, verdict prediction) that directly matches this proposal's architecture
FacTeR-Check (Borrego-Obrador et al., 2023) implements semi-automated fact-checking via semantic similarity and NLI, covering extraction-to-verdict pipeline
ClaimBuster system already implements a four-component pipeline (claim monitor, claim spotter, claim matcher, claim checker) nearly identical to the proposed design
Multiple LLM-based fact-checking systems exist (2024-2026) combining retrieval with parametric knowledge for automated verification
